{
  "workings":"The negative effects of monoculture farming on biodiversity are: 1) It reduces species richness by replacing diverse habitats with a single crop, eliminating many plant and animal species. 2) It increases vulnerability to pests and diseases, which leads farmers to use more pesticides and herbicides that harm non‑target organisms. 3) Repeated planting of the same crop depletes soil health and microbial diversity, reducing the range of soil organisms. 4) It causes genetic erosion because local and wild varieties are displaced by uniform commercial strains. 5) It disrupts ecosystem services such as pollination, natural pest control and nutrient cycling, further harming biodiversity.",
